page: Microsoft Azure D4alds_v7 is a virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided via a local 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression tests all scoring in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks also register average performance, as do Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and small-model LLM inference. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25%.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2, this instance offers a compute-focused hardware profile. It provides a cost-efficient option for workloads that require high single-threaded CPU performance but have modest memory footprints. The inclusion of a local NVMe SSD provides fast temporary storage. This server is suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, software compilation, and basic database operations that fit within the 8.0 GB memory limit.
description: Microsoft Azure D4alds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Configured with 8.0 GB of memory and a local 236 GB NVMe SSD, this instance offers a compute-optimized 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU performance, single-threaded text processing, and compression capabilities, while multi-core operations and memory bandwidth perform at average levels. The instance lacks GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy, low-memory workloads. It is suited for tasks such as single-threaded data processing, software compilation, lightweight web serving, and database operations that do not exceed the memory capacity.
